note: FD.74 (edge audit A2, FD.3c; residual of FD.4b). A SQL / Cypher statement literal is a data access only as the argument of a call that runs it: never the content of a file write (`std::fs::write(p, "CREATE TABLE ..")`, a local `write(dir, rel, body)` helper, `Path.write_text(..)`, `fs.writeFileSync(..)`), never a query to glia's in-process evaluator (`g.query_gql("MATCH ..")`), and (FD.6's rule completed) never inside a Cargo test / bench target file. Baseline HEAD 77ddc286: forbid violations 8. Controls: Rust `client.query`, Python `conn.execute` / `session.run`, a Dart StringBuffer `sql.write(..)` builder (the content is the FIRST argument, so a buffer write keeps), and a Python test that seeds a table (Python has no test-scope rule).
